title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 363 (Settlement of claims of creditors by Official Liquidator)

content.overview: The Official Liquidator shall, within thirty days of his appointment or such further period as the Tribunal may allow, call upon the creditors to prove their claims in such manner as may be prescribed. The Official Liquidator shall settle the claims of creditors and prepare a list of creditors. Any creditor aggrieved by the decision of the Official Liquidator may appeal to the Tribunal within thirty days of the decision.
content.glance: Official Liquidator calls for proofs within 30 days (or further time allowed), settles claims and prepares list of creditors; aggrieved creditors may appeal to Tribunal within 30 days.
content.study: Section 363 governs creditor claims in Official Liquidator administrations. Within thirty days of appointment (or such further period as the Tribunal allows), the Official Liquidator must call upon creditors to prove their claims in the prescribed manner, settle the claims and prepare a list of creditors. A creditor aggrieved by the Official Liquidator’s decision may appeal to the Tribunal within thirty days of that decision.
